source_text: Πάντ̓ οὖν ἤδη παῤ ἑαυτῷ σὺν τῷ παιδὶ οἰκονομηκώς, μέχρι μὲν τοῦ πρόσθεν χρόνου εἴασεν ἡμᾶς, ὡς ἐβουλόμεθα, ἀτάκτοις φοραῖς φέρεσθαι, ἡδοναῖς καὶ ἐπιθυμίαις ἀπαγομένους. οὐ πάντως ἐφηδόμενος τοῖς ἁμαρτήμασιν ἡμῶν, ἀλλ’ ἀνεχόμενος, οὐδὲ τῷ τότε τῆς ἀδικίας καιρῷ συνευδοκῶν, ἀλλὰ τὸν νῦν τῆς δικαιοσύνης δημιουργῶν, ἵνα ἐν τῷ τότε χρόνῳ ἐλεγχθέντες ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων ἔργων ἀνάξιοι ζωῆς νῦν ὑπὸ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ χρηστότητος ἀξιωθῶμεν, καὶ τὸ καθ̓ ἑαυτοὺς φανερώσαντες ἀδύνατον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ θεοῦ δυνατοὶ γενηθῶμεν. ἐπεὶ δὲ πεπλήρωτο μὲν ἡ ἡμετέρα ἀδικία καὶ τελείως πεφανέρωτο, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς αὐτῆς κόλασις καὶ θάνατος προσεδοκᾶτο, ἦλθε δὲ ὁ καιρός, ὃν θεὸς προέθετο λοιπὸν φανερῶσαι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ χρηστότητα καὶ δύναμιν ʽὢ τῆς ὑπερβαλλούσης φιλανθρωπίας καὶ ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοὖ, οὐκ ἐμίσησεν ἡμᾶς οὐδὲ ἀπώσατο οὐδὲ ἐμνησικάκησεν, ἀλλὰ ἐμακροθύμησεν, ἠνέσχετο, ἐλεῶν αὐτὸς τὰς ἡμετέρας ἁμαρτίας ἀνεδέξατο, αὐτὸς τὸν ἴδιον υἱὸν ἀπέδοτο λύτρον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τὸν ἅγιον ὑπὲρ ἀνόμων, τὸν ἄκακον ὑπὲρ τῶν κακῶν, τὸν δίκαιον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδίκων, τὸν ἄφθαρτον ὑπὲρ τῶν φθαρτῶν, τὸν ἀθάνατον ὑπὲρ τῶν θνητῶν. τί γὰρ ἄλλο τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν ἠδυνήθη καλύψαι ἢ ἐκείνου δικαιοσύνη; ἐν τίνι δικαιωθῆναι δυνατὸν τοὺς ἀνόμους ἡμᾶς καὶ ἀσεβεῖς ἢ ἐν μόνῳ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ; ὢ τῆς γλυκείας ἀνταλλαγῆς, ὢ τῆς ἀνεξιχνιάστου δημιουργίας, ὢ τῶν ἀπροσδοκήτων εὐεργεσιῶν: ἵνα ἀνομία μὲν πολλῶν ἐν δικαίῳ ἑνὶ κρυβῇ, δικαιοσύνη δὲ ἑνὸς πολλοὺς ἀνόμους δικαιώσῃ. ἐλέγξας οὖν ἐν μὲν τῷ πρόσθεν χρόνῳ τὸ ἀδύνατον τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως εἰς τὸ τυχεῖν ζωῆς, νῦν δὲ τὸν σωτῆρα δείξας δυνατὸν σώζειν καὶ τὰ ἀδύνατα, ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων ἐβουλήθη πιστεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ χρηστότητι αὐτοῦ, αὐτὸν ἡγεῖσθαι τροφέα, πατέρα, διδάσκαλον, σύμβουλον, ἰατρόν, νοῦν, φῶς, τιμήν, δόξαν, ἰσχύν, ζωήν, περὶ ἐνδύσεως καὶ τροφῆς μὴ μεριμνᾶν.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore God having already managed everything with His child, until the former time He allowed us, as we wished, to be carried away with disorderly impulses, being led by pleasures and desires. Not being at all pleased with our sins, but tolerating them, nor at that time consenting to the season of injustice, but now creating righteousness, so that having been convicted in that time by our own works as unworthy of life, we might now be deemed worthy by the kindness of God, and having shown ourselves to be unable to enter the kingdom of God by our own power, we might become able by the power of God. And since our injustice had been fulfilled and had been fully revealed, that the reward of it is punishment and death, and the time came, which God had foreordained to reveal His own kindness and power, oh the surpassing philanthropy and love of God, He did not hate us, nor did He reject us, nor did He hold a grudge, but He was long-suffering, He endured, He had pity, He Himself received our sins, He gave His own Son as a ransom for us, the Holy One for the lawless, the Innocent for the wicked, the Righteous for the unrighteous, the Immortal for the mortal. For what else could cover our sins except His righteousness? In what else could the lawless and ungodly ones like us be justified except in the only Son of God? Oh the sweet exchange, oh the unfathomable creation, oh the unexpected benefits: that the lawlessness of many might be hidden in one righteous person, and the righteousness of one might justify many lawless ones. Having convicted us, therefore, in the former time of the inability of our nature to attain life, and now having shown the Savior to be able to save even the unable, He wished us to trust in His kindness, to consider Him our nourisher, father, teacher, counselor, physician, mind, light, honor, glory, strength, life, and not to worry about clothing and food.
pass_b_english: God has already ordered everything with His Son. Until the former time, He let us be carried along by our own disordered impulses, led by pleasures and desires, just as we wished. He did this not because He took any pleasure in our sins, but because He tolerated them. He was not consenting to that season of injustice; rather, He was preparing the present season of righteousness. His purpose was that, after we had been convicted in that earlier time by our own works as unworthy of life, we might now be deemed worthy by God's kindness. And after we had shown ourselves unable to enter God's kingdom by our own power, we might become able by God's power.

Now our injustice has reached its full measure and has been fully revealed, so that its wage — punishment and death — was expected. Then came the time God had foreordained to reveal His own kindness and power. Oh, the surpassing philanthropy and love of God! He did not hate us, nor reject us, nor hold a grudge. Instead, He was long-suffering; He endured; He had pity. He Himself took our sins upon Himself. He gave His own Son as a ransom for us — the Holy One for the lawless, the Innocent for the wicked, the Righteous for the unrighteous, the Immortal for the mortal, the Undying for the dying. For what else could cover our sins but His righteousness? In whom could we lawless and ungodly ones be justified except in the only Son of God? Oh, the sweet exchange! Oh, the unfathomable creation! Oh, the unexpected benefits! The lawlessness of many is hidden in one righteous person, and the righteousness of one justifies many lawless ones.

Therefore, having convicted us in the former time of our nature's inability to attain life, and now having shown the Savior able to save even the unable, God willed that we trust in His kindness from both experiences. He wants us to regard Him as our nourisher, father, teacher, counselor, physician, mind, light, honor, glory, strength, and life — and not to worry about clothing and food.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the complex causal and temporal relationships. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source. The distinction between 'the Immortal for the mortal' (Pass A) and 'the Undying for the dying' (Pass B) is a valid stylistic variation of 'τὸν ἄφθαρτον ὑπὲρ τῶν θνητῶν'.

Pass A and Pass B accurately reflect the Greek text. The translation preserves the meaning, agency, and theological concepts. Scripture citations are not present in the text, so no issues there. The title 'God's Plan for Humanity' appropriately captures the content of the passage.
